territorial_scope.description: Applies to the Department of Defense and other federal agencies within the United States.

evidence.quote: The Secretary of Defense shall delegate to the Director of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center the acquisition authority

summary.short: FY2021 NDAA sections on AI in the Department of Defense and federal government: JAIC acquisition authority (sunset 1 October 2025), JAIC advisory board, AI workforce hiring and pay, pilots, studies and reports, and deepfake-forgery reporting. Addressed to the Secretary of Defense and federal agencies.
summary.long: Selected AI-related sections of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act. Sec. 808 gives the Director of the Joint Artificial Intelligence Center (JAIC) acquisition authority of an agency head, a JAIC acquisition executive, at least 10 full-time staff, and a $75,000,000 cap per fiscal year on new contracts, with the authority sunsetting on 1 October 2025. Secs. 231-233 amend JAIC reporting and create a board of advisors. Secs. 234 and 235 require AI use-case identification, prototyping, and an assessment of ethically developed AI acquisition. Sec. 236 permits a steering committee on emerging technology until 1 October 2024. Sec. 1751 directs the Secretary of Defense to review and issue hiring guidance for AI professionals. Secs. 241 and 247-249 set proficiency tests, incentive pay, electronic-portfolio and self-directed training pilots, and part-time faculty and student employment. Sec. 513 authorizes STEM grants covering AI for JROTC units. Secs. 9004 and 589F require reports or studies on digital content forgery and deepfakes. Secs. 9407, 9412 and 9414 address national cybersecurity challenges, an industries-of-the-future council, and a study of Chinese influence on international standards. Other sections cover spectrum IT modernization, unmanned systems, and AI use by FinCEN.

thresholds.value_text: may not obligate or expend more than $75,000,000 out of the funds made available in each of fiscal years 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024, and 2025
thresholds.measurement: per fiscal year, measured against funds made available in each of fiscal years 2021 through 2025; applies to new contracts supporting acquisition activities under this section
thresholds.consequence: Caps the Director's obligations and expenditures for new contracts under the Sec. 808(a) acquisition authority at $75,000,000 per fiscal year in the listed years.
thresholds.conditions: Applies in exercising the acquisition authority granted in subsection (a); limited to new contracts to support appropriate acquisition activities carried out under this section.

thresholds.variable_text: special pay rate for programming language proficiency (10 U.S.C. 1596c(b))
thresholds.value_text: may not exceed 20 percent of the employee’s rate of basic pay
thresholds.measurement: rate prescribed by the Secretary of Defense, expressed as a share of the individual employee's rate of basic pay
thresholds.consequence: Sets a ceiling of 20 percent of basic pay on the special pay rate for certified DoD civilian employees with programming language proficiency.
thresholds.conditions: Employee certified by the Secretary as proficient in a programming language identified as necessary for national security, and assigned duties requiring that proficiency.
